parsed.narrative: The default analysis reports a conversion lift of +0.53 pp (95% CI +0.14 to +0.92, p = 0.008) across 29,926 sessions, which clears the rule and says SHIP. The minimal flip changes Internal traffic from "Keep all sessions" to "Exclude internal accounts". That lift does not survive one defensible decision. 339 sessions come from internal accounts (employees and QA), 76% of them landed in the treatment arm, and 59% of them converted because they were test orders. Excluding internal accounts leaves 29,587 sessions and a lift of -0.14 pp (95% CI -0.50 to +0.21, p = 0.434), which says DON'T SHIP. This is the single decision that moves the estimate most (0.67 pp); the next largest, 0.26 pp, leaves the verdict unchanged.
caveats: Influence is measured by switching one decision at a time from the defaults; it is a statement about this analysis, not a causal claim about the world.
The no-effect reading rests on the 339 flagged sessions being test traffic; confirm the is_internal flag with the data owner.
Excluding internal accounts does not prove the new checkout has no effect, only that the data cannot distinguish it from zero.
